summary:
MARS GODS EYE is a prototype route planner and 3D mission viewer for simulated Mars exploration, featuring an astronaut, a rover, and a drone. Orbital terrain models provide essential context but cannot resolve every local hazard. The CTX terrain model used at Jezero, for example, has elevation samples spaced 20 m apart.
Our planner uses public NASA/USGS orbital terrain as an estimated map, preserving its uncertainty and provenance. It evaluates FAST or SAFE candidate routes against explicit models of time, energy, and astronaut oxygen consumption, including travel, planned work, return, and reserves. Controlled single-astronaut ROS tests demonstrate stopping, invalidating an affected route, and replanning from the current position and remaining resources after a simulated terrain contradiction. Recorded mission events and routes can be replayed in a compatible web browser without a running ROS backend.
The viewer offers six illustrative environments using public Mars terrain and imagery: Jezero, Gale and Gusev craters, Meridiani Planum, Elysium Planitia and Valles Marineris. Real rover traverse data are included where available; mission stories and local observations are explicitly simulated. Full three-agent mission validation remains ongoing. Our prototype explores how uncertain orbital estimates can be refined by local observations to support resource-aware exploration.
